react.observe: First cycle. Starting with $500,000 USDT, no positions. Three meme token pools exist: SHADOW/USDT (price $0.01), ROCKET/USDT (price ~$0.00106), MOON/USDT (price ~$0.0258). Oracle prices: ETH $2800, SOL $150, BTC $95000. GoldenWhale launched ROCKET with $10k liquidity. Multiple retail traders (HappyTrader, DiamondHands, LeverageKing) bought ETH and meme tokens. CryptoGuru bullish on MOON. ShadowTrader is cryptic. BearKing bearish. LiquidKiller sees stability. AlphaBot looking for pairs. No V3 LP positions yet — no fees being collected.
react.think: As a market maker with minting power, my primary edge is: (1) earning fees from LP positions, (2) strategic liquidity positioning, (3) minting tokens to create inventory. The meme token pools (SHADOW, ROCKET, MOON) have existing liquidity and retail traders are actively buying them. If I add liquidity to these pools, I earn 0.3% fees on every swap. ROCKET is being hyped by GoldenWhale — retail is buying in. MOON is being pushed by CryptoGuru. This means swap volume will be HIGH in these pools. I should add liquidity to all three meme pools to capture fees from the retail buying frenzy. I also need to consider: I have no ETH/SOL/BTC to add to those pools directly. I could mint some tokens to seed liquidity. For meme pools, I need the respective token + USDT. I can mint SHADOW, MOON, ROCKET... wait, those were created by other agents. I can only mint ETH, SOL, BTC via the mint API. So for meme pools, I'd need to buy the tokens first or swap into them. Actually, looking at the v3_add_liquidity mechanic — I need to provide both sides of liquidity. I should: 1) Add liquidity to ROCKET/USDT pool (high volume incoming from hype), 2) Add liquidity to MOON/USDT pool, 3) Add liquidity to SHADOW/USDT pool. But I need the tokens. I can swap USDT for these tokens first via v3_swap, then add liquidity. Alternatively, I could just add one-sided liquidity above/below current price. Actually in V3, you can add liquidity in a range — if the range is entirely above current price, you only need token0; if entirely below, you only need token1 (USDT). Let me think about this: current ROCKET price is ~$0.00106. If I add liquidity in a range ABOVE current price (say ticks above current), I only need USDT. When price moves up (as people buy ROCKET), my liquidity gets utilized and I earn fees. This is a valid strategy. For MOON at ~$0.0258, same approach. Let me calculate rough ticks. For ROCKET at price 0.00106: tick = ln(sqrt(0.00106))/ln(1.0001) ≈ -68537 (matches pool). For adding liquidity above current price, I'd pick tickLower = -68537 (current) to tickUpper = -60000 (higher price). This range would require USDT to be deployed. Actually in V3: if current tick is below tickLower, position holds token0 only. If current tick is above tickUpper, position holds token1 only. If current tick is within range, holds both. Since retail is buying (price moving UP), I want liquidity IN the current range to capture fees immediately. I'll add liquidity around current price for all three pools. I need to swap some USDT into each token first. Let me plan: allocate ~$50k to each pool ($150k total for meme pools), keep $350k for ETH/BTC pool liquidity or future opportunities. Strategy: swap $5k USDT for each meme token, then add concentrated liquidity around current prices.
